facts.text: A scenario describes a situation unfolding over time at one of three levels: functional scenarios use words, logical scenarios use parameter ranges, and concrete scenarios fix every value.
facts.quote: A scenario is a description of a situation that unfolds over time, written at one of three levels of detail: in words (functional), with parameter ranges (logical), or with every value fixed (concrete).

facts.text: Scenario-based testing, rather than hours of random driving, was the backbone of every documented on-road and off-road validation program the booklet found.
facts.quote: Testing against scenarios, rather than against hours of random driving, is the backbone of every documented validation program the booklet found, on-road and off-road [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The functional, logical and concrete scenario levels originated in the German PEGASUS research project and were adopted into ISO 34501 to ISO 34505.
facts.quote: The three levels come from the German PEGASUS research project and were adopted into the ISO 34501 to 34505 standards [Chapter 9].

facts.text: EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) provides the mining storyboard “vehicle reversing towards a person” as an example of a functional scenario.
facts.quote: A functional scenario is the story in plain language, such as the mining industry's EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) storyboard "vehicle reversing towards a person".

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: The glossary's logical scenario example varies person distance from 0 to 30 m, approach angle, machine speed from 0 to 15 km/h, and dust density from clear to heavy.
facts.quote: A logical scenario keeps the story but replaces the details with ranges: person distance 0 to 30 m, approach angle, machine speed 0 to 15 km/h, dust density from clear to heavy.

facts.text: Concrete scenarios are executed by simulators or test tracks; logical scenarios are sampled by statisticians; functional scenarios communicate the situation to regulators or mine managers.
facts.quote: A concrete scenario is what a simulator or a test track actually runs; a logical scenario is what statisticians sample from; a functional scenario is what a regulator or a mine manager understands [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The booklet anchors scenario content in off-road standards ISO 21815-1:2022 and ISO 21815-3:2023, which define detection, warning and intervention for forward and reverse motion.
facts.quote: the booklet anchors on the off-road standards: ISO 21815-1:2022 and ISO 21815-3:2023 define detection, warning and intervention for forward and reverse motion

facts.text: Parts 4 and 5 of ISO 21815 address swing and other motions.
facts.quote: with swing and other motions in Parts 4 and 5

facts.text: EMESRT PR-5A storyboards supply mining hazard patterns traceable to known fatal accidents for scenario content.
facts.quote: the EMESRT PR-5A storyboards supply the mining hazard patterns that are traceable to known fatal accidents [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The off-road standards and EMESRT PR-5A storyboards used for scenario content cover only situations that experts thought of.
facts.quote: Their weaknesses are that they cover only what experts thought of

facts.text: The off-road standards and EMESRT PR-5A storyboards used for scenario content do not specify how often each situation occurs.
facts.quote: say nothing about how often each situation occurs

facts.text: The off-road standards and EMESRT PR-5A storyboards used for scenario content are not machine-readable.
facts.quote: and are not machine-readable [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Off-road scenarios have no lanes, so positions must be expressed in world or machine coordinates.
facts.quote: There are no lanes, so positions must be expressed in world or machine coordinates.

facts.text: Normal off-road tasks that look like collisions include driving into a pile, backing to a dump edge and working beside a spotter.
facts.quote: And many normal tasks look like collisions: driving into a pile, backing to a dump edge, working beside a spotter [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The illustrated functional scenario describes a loader reversing from a stockpile toward a worker who does not move away; its logical family varies speed from 0 to 15 km/h, distance from 0 to 30 m, approach angle, dust density, slope and load.
facts.quote:
F["Functional scenario, in words: a loader reverses from a stockpile toward a worker who does not move away"]
    L["Logical scenario, with ranges: speed 0 to 15 km/h, distance 0 to 30 m, approach angle, dust density, slope, load"]

facts.text: Illustrated concrete scenario A uses 9 km/h speed, 12 m distance, a 30-degree approach angle, moderate dust, a 4% grade and a loaded machine.
facts.quote: Concrete scenario A: 9 km/h, 12 m, 30 degrees, moderate dust, 4% grade, loaded

facts.text: Illustrated concrete scenario B uses 14 km/h speed, 25 m distance, a 0-degree approach angle, clear air, flat terrain and an empty machine.
facts.quote: Concrete scenario B: 14 km/h, 25 m, 0 degrees, clear air, flat, empty

facts.text: Illustrated concrete scenario C uses 5 km/h speed, 6 m distance, a 60-degree approach angle, heavy dust, an 8% grade and a loaded machine.
facts.quote: Concrete scenario C: 5 km/h, 6 m, 60 degrees, heavy dust, 8% grade, loaded

facts.text: One functional scenario becomes one logical family with ranges, yielding as many concrete test runs as the test campaign needs.
facts.quote: one functional story becomes one logical family with ranges, which yields as many concrete test runs as the campaign needs.

facts.text: The scenario catalog guarantees that known fatal-accident patterns are always tested.
facts.quote: The scenario catalog guarantees that known fatal-accident patterns are always tested

facts.text: Logical scenarios make thousands of virtual runs and a statistical claim possible.
facts.quote: the logical level is what makes thousands of virtual runs and a statistical claim possible

facts.text: The booklet places scenario definition in the first program phase, before sensor selection.
facts.quote: the booklet puts scenario definition in the first phase, before the sensor is chosen [Chapters 1, 9].
